One node of a tree, which is either an element or a run of text. What every node has in common is where it sits: its parent, its root, how deep it is, and a revision that says when anything under it last changed.

The revision is one number for every tree in the game. Whatever draws a tree keeps the number it last laid out at and compares, so a frame where nothing moved costs no layout at all.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.client.dom.DOMTreeNode;
```

### `public static void touch()`

Called by anything that changes what layout would come out as.

### `public void touched()`

Marks this node and everything above it as changed, so a box worked out for an element that was left alone can be used again while the ones around it are laid out afresh.
